instruction:
Fix `plugins/scaffolder-react/src/next/lib/schema.ts` for these problems, changing only what they need, following the conventions in the shared brief:
1. Gate 3 defects 1-4 in resolveStepSchema (reproduced by calling resolveStepSchema / findSchemaForKey + isKeyDefinedInSchemas directly). Let platform = { title: 'Platform', type: 'string', enum: ['ios', 'android'] }. Common root: a branch property that is a real field (it has type, title, items, properties, ui:field, ui:widget or any keyword besides const/enum) is treated as a condition/discriminator key just because it has enum or const. Fix: only a pure constraint (an object whose only keywords are const and/or enum) is ever a discriminator or condition key; a real field never is, whatever enum/const it has. Defects: (1) buildBranchTestSchema (line ~292) counts `platform` as a discriminator via `!ownKeys.has(k) && ('const' in v || 'enum' in v)`, puts it in the test schema's required, and discriminatorKeys excludes it from the merge. Step 2 `{ properties: { sdkName: { type: 'string' } }, dependencies: { toggle: { oneOf: [ { properties: { toggle: { const: true }, platform }, required: ['platform'] }, { properties: { toggle: { const: false } } } ] } } }` with `resolveStepSchema(schema, { toggle: true }, { previousStepKeys: new Set(['toggle']) })` returns properties [sdkName] only; expected sdkName and platform, with required ['platform']. (2) getBranchConditionKeys (line ~222) recurses into then/else and counts `platform` as a condition key. Condition keys come only from `if` (its properties and required) and from pure-constraint discriminator properties of oneOf/anyOf branches, never from then/else contents. Repro: `{ properties: { includeName: { type: 'boolean' } }, dependencies: { includeName: { allOf: [ { if: { properties: { includeName: { const: true } } }, then: { properties: { lastName: { type: 'string' }, platform } } } ] } } }` with `{ includeName: true, lastName: 'Doe', platform: 'ios' }` and resolveAll: true returns [includeName, lastName]; expected platform too. (3) Root-level oneOf without discriminators: `{ type: 'object', oneOf: [ { title: 'New repo', properties: { repoName: { type: 'string' } }, required: ['repoName'] }, { title: 'Existing repo', properties: { existingRepo: { type: 'string' } }, required: ['existingRepo'] } ] }` with `{ existingRepo: 'org/repo' }` and resolveAll: true returns [repoName]; expected [existingRepo]. With no discriminators every test schema is `{ type: 'object' }`, so the first branch always matches. Match a branch the way rjsf's own option matching does (node_modules/@rjsf/utils/lib/schema/getMatchingOption.js lines 43-56): test the branch augmented with `anyOf: Object.keys(branch.properties).map(key => ({ required: [key] }))` (wrapped in allOf when the branch already has anyOf), so it matches only when the data holds at least one of its properties and validates; if no branch matches, use the first branch as today. (4) mergeBranchIntoSchema (line ~348) lifts if/then onto the target only when target[keyword] === undefined, so with resolveAll: false `{ properties: { flag: { type: 'boolean' }, mode: { type: 'string' } }, allOf: [ { if: { properties: { flag: { const: true } }, required: ['flag'] }, then: { properties: { platform } } }, { if: { properties: { mode: { const: 'x' } }, required: ['mode'] }, then: { properties: { region: { title: 'Region', type: 'string', enum: ['eu', 'us'] } } } } ] }` and `{ flag: true, mode: 'x' }` keeps only the flag item; the mode/region item is dropped. Never drop a conditional: when the target already holds that keyword, keep the item (for example append it to target.allOf). Keep same-step conditionals unresolved when resolveAll is false (both allOf items are same-step here), keep standard JSON Schema semantics (dependencies apply whenever the key is present, only undefined skips), keep a step's own top-level properties, and change nothing else.
